Title: Why is my monthly bill higher than the estimate in my proposal?
Summary: Common reasons a Brightline invoice exceeds the original production estimate, and how to check each one.
Question__c: My proposal said I'd pay about $118/month. My last two invoices were $164 and $171. Why?
Answer__c:
Short answer

Your invoice has two parts: the fixed financing payment (which never changes) and the utility true-up for any power you drew from the grid. The second part is what moves.

Check these first

  1. Production vs. estimate. Open Brightline Home → Reports → Monthly Production and compare to the proposal. Anything below 85% of estimate for two months in a row should be reported as low production.
  2. Usage increase. A new EV charger, heat pump, or pool pump can add 300–600 kWh/month.
  3. Utility rate change. Most utilities adjusted time-of-use rates in the last 12 months. Your true-up is billed at the utility's current rate, not the rate in the proposal.
  4. Shading or soiling. See cleaning your panels.
Line itemChanges month to month?Where to check
Financing paymentNoLoan agreement
Utility true-upYesUtility bill, page 2
Monitoring subscriptionOnly at renewalAccount → Plan

Note: Brightline does not bill you for grid power. That charge comes from your utility; we show it in the app for convenience.

Title: What do the alert colors in Brightline Home mean?
Summary: Meaning of green, amber, and red system status and which alerts need action.
Question__c: My app shows an amber dot. Do I need to do something?
Answer__c:
ColorMeaningAction
GreenProducing normallyNone
AmberProducing, but below expected, or one inverter offlineWatch for 48 hours; if it persists, report it
RedNo production for 24+ hours during daylightRun the inverter restart, then contact support
GreyNo data receivedCheck Wi-Fi; see reconnect the gateway

Amber during heavy cloud cover, snow, or the first week after install is normal.

Title: What are the Partner API rate limits?
Summary: Request limits per tier, the headers returned, and how to handle 429 responses.
Question__c: We're getting HTTP 429 from the sites endpoint. What are the limits?
Answer__c:
TierRequests / minuteRequests / day

Every response includes:

X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 412

On a 429, wait until X-RateLimit-Reset (Unix seconds) and retry. Bulk production history should use the bulk export endpoint, which is not rate-limited per request.

Title: Set up autopay
Summary: Enroll a bank account or card for automatic monthly payments.
Procedure_Body__c:
Before you start: have your bank routing and account number, or a card, ready. Autopay drafts on the 10th of each month.

Steps

  1. Open Brightline Home and go to Billing → Payment methods.
  2. Tap Add payment method and choose Bank account or Card.
  3. Enter the details and tap Verify. Bank accounts receive two micro-deposits within 2 business days; return to this screen to confirm the amounts.
  4. Once verified, toggle Use for autopay.
  5. Confirm the authorization text and tap Enable autopay.

To turn autopay off

Return to Payment methods, open the method, and toggle Use for autopay off. Do this at least 3 business days before the 10th to avoid that month's draft.

Title: Enable two-factor authentication
Summary: Add an authenticator app or SMS code to your login.
Procedure_Body__c:
1. Go to Account → Security.
  2. Tap Two-factor authentication → Set up.
  3. Choose Authenticator app (recommended) or SMS.
  4. Scan the QR code or enter the phone number, then enter the 6-digit code.
  5. Save your backup codes. You'll need one if you lose your phone.

Warning: enabling 2FA signs you out of all devices, including household members' devices.

Title: Restart your inverter
Summary: Safe power-cycle procedure for the inverter when the app shows a red alert.
Procedure_Body__c:
Safety: do not open any enclosure. This procedure only uses the external switches and breakers.

Steps

  1. Locate the AC disconnect (grey box next to your utility meter) and switch it OFF.
  2. Locate the DC disconnect on the inverter and switch it OFF.
  3. Wait 5 minutes. The inverter display will go dark.
  4. Switch the DC disconnect ON.
  5. Switch the AC disconnect ON.
  6. Wait up to 10 minutes for the inverter to reconnect to the grid. The display should show a production reading.

If the alert persists after 30 minutes, submit a service request.

Title: Get a Partner API access token
Summary: OAuth client credentials flow for server-to-server integrations.
Procedure_Body__c:
Prerequisite: a Partner API application with a client ID and secret from the Partner Portal.

Request

POST https://api.brightlinesolar.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=YOUR_ID&client_secret=YOUR_SECRET&scope=sites:read production:read

Response

{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 3600
}

Cache the token and refresh it before expiry. Tokens are not revoked on rotation of the secret for 10 minutes, giving you a rollover window.

Next: Partner API overview.

Title: Export production history in bulk
Summary: Use the asynchronous export endpoint for large date ranges.
Procedure_Body__c:
1. Create a job: 
    POST /v2/exports
{ "site_ids": ["..."], "from": "2025-01-01", "to": "2025-12-31", "granularity": "hourly" }
  2. Poll GET /v2/exports/{id} until status is ready. Typical wait: 30–120 seconds.
  3. Download download_url (a signed URL valid for 1 hour). Files are gzipped CSV.

Jobs are limited to 500 sites and 3 years each. Export jobs do not count against the per-request rate limit.

Title: Set up a webhook for alert events
Summary: Receive alert.opened and alert.closed events instead of polling.
Procedure_Body__c:
1. Register an endpoint: 
    POST /v2/webhooks
{ "url": "https://example.com/hooks/brightline", "events": ["alert.opened", "alert.closed", "site.pto"] }
  2. Store the returned signing_secret.
  3. Verify each delivery by computing HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body with the secret and comparing to the X-Brightline-Signature header.
  4. Respond with 2xx within 5 seconds. Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff for 24 hours.

Payload example:

{
  "event": "alert.opened",
  "site_id": "st_48a1",
  "severity": "red",
  "occurred_at": "2026-06-12T14:03:00Z"
}

Title: New In-App Weather Delay Tracker Now Live in Brightline Home
Summary: Brightline Home now includes a real-time weather delay tracker so customers can monitor their installation status and expected reschedule timeline without calling support.
Abstract__c: As of March 3, 2025, customers with an upcoming installation appointment can open the Brightline Home app and view a live weather delay status card that shows the specific condition causing any hold, the estimated window for rescheduling, and a direct link to accept or decline a newly offered date — all without contacting support.
Body__c:
Brightline Solar launched the Weather Delay Tracker inside the Brightline Home app on March 3, 2025. The tracker is visible to any customer whose installation appointment falls within the next 14 calendar days.

Where to find it

Open Brightline Home → tap My Project → select Appointment Details → scroll to the Weather Status card.

Status indicators

StatusMeaning
On ScheduleNo weather concerns detected for your window
WatchBorderline conditions; monitoring hourly
DelayedAppointment cancelled; reschedule offer pending
RescheduledNew date confirmed; tap to accept

Customers have 24 hours to accept a rescheduled date through the app before the slot is released. If no action is taken, the system will auto-assign the next available date and send a confirmation. A reschedule offer declined twice within the same delay event will require a manual call to the Scheduling team (reference code WD-MANUAL).

For same-day arrival window communications related to your rescheduled appointment, see Same-Day Crew Arrival Window Updates.

Title: Lifetime Stats Endpoint Launches in Brightline Partner API
Summary: Partners can now retrieve cumulative lifetime production and savings data for any authorized site via the new GET /v2/sites/{site_id}/stats/lifetime endpoint, available as of August 11, 2025.
Abstract__c: Brightline's Partner API now exposes lifetime performance statistics through a dedicated endpoint, allowing integration partners to surface long-term generation, savings, and CO₂ offset data in their own dashboards without manually aggregating daily or monthly report records.
Body__c:
Endpoint Details

The new endpoint is available in API v2 only and requires the sites:stats:read OAuth2 scope.

GET /v2/sites/{site_id}/stats/lifetime

Response Fields

FieldTypeDescription
total_generation_kwhnumberCumulative AC output since activation
estimated_savings_usdnumberDollar savings at blended rate on record
co2_offset_metric_tonsnumberCO₂ avoided using EPA eGrid regional factor
data_through_dateISO 8601 dateMost recent date included in totals

Rate Limits & Caching

The endpoint is rate-limited to 120 requests per minute per OAuth client. Lifetime totals are recalculated nightly; polling more frequently than once every 24 hours is unnecessary and will count against your quota.

Error Handling

A 404 Site Not Found response indicates the site_id is not authorized under your OAuth token. For guidance on handling unexpected 4xx responses, see Interpret 4xx Error Codes in the Partner API. This endpoint went live on August 11, 2025 and is not back-ported to API v1.

Title: Neighbor Comparison Data Now Available via the Brightline Partner API
Summary: Partners can now retrieve anonymized neighborhood benchmark production data for enrolled sites using the new /v1/sites/{site_id}/neighbor-comparison endpoint, launched February 3, 2026.
Abstract__c: Alongside the consumer-facing Neighbor Comparison feature in Brightline Home, Brightline's Partner API now exposes the same benchmarking dataset through a dedicated REST endpoint. Available to all OAuth2-authenticated partners with the reports:read scope, the endpoint returns aggregated median, 25th-percentile, and 75th-percentile production figures for the anonymized peer group matched to a given site, enabling partners to surface actionable benchmarking insights inside their own dashboards and customer-facing tools.
Body__c:
Endpoint Details

Released February 3, 2026, the new endpoint is:

GET /v1/sites/{site_id}/neighbor-comparison

Required OAuth2 Scope

reports:read — no additional scope approval is needed if your application already holds this permission.

Query Parameters

ParameterTypeRequiredDescription
periodstringYes"monthly" or "annual"
yearintegerYes4-digit year, e.g. 2025
monthintegerNo1–12; required if period=monthly

Response Fields

  • peer_median_kwh — median output of the matched peer group
  • peer_p25_kwh — 25th percentile
  • peer_p75_kwh — 75th percentile
  • site_output_kwh — the enrolled site's actual output
  • peer_count — number of anonymized households in the comparison

Error Codes

If fewer than 8 peer households match the site, the API returns HTTP 422 with error code NEIGHBOR_PEER_POOL_TOO_SMALL. For general 4xx guidance, see Partner API 4xx Error Code Reference.

Rate limits follow standard Partner API policy: 120 requests per minute per client credential.
